title: Unify CrowdStrike Falcon security context with Dynatrace runtime insights for faster incident resolution
summary: Unify CrowdStrike Falcon detections with Dynatrace runtime context to see if a threat caused an outage and prioritize fixes.
body_markdown:
Dynatrace integrates with the CrowdStrike Falcon platform to bring CrowdStrike detection findings and threat intelligence into Dynatrace. The integration enriches CrowdStrike security data with Dynatrace runtime context, helping SRE and security teams investigate affected services and coordinate responses.


Dynatrace and CrowdStrike each have a clear role. CrowdStrike is the security enforcement layer: it detects threats and responds to them, for example by isolating a host. Dynatrace provides continuous runtime observability context, watching for drift, anomalies, and patterns across your environment. When CrowdStrike findings land in Dynatrace, they are automatically enriched with runtime context. Security and SRE teams can then decide on guardrails and response using the full picture of what the affected services are doing, not an individual security finding.


Dynatrace observes telemetry across the full stack, including hybrid, cloud, and AI workloads. You can therefore investigate CrowdStrike findings in the context of the services and infrastructure they touch, wherever they run.


## How does the CrowdStrike integration help you understand why a service became unavailable?


When a critical service goes down, SRE teams benefit from instantly knowing that CrowdStrike may have isolated the underlying host in response to a security threat.


1. Dynatrace alerts you that a critical service is unavailable, and problem analysis points to a host that is no longer reachable.
2. When you investigate that host, the CrowdStrike detection, automatically enriched with runtime entities in Dynatrace, appears as the cause of the host going down and shows that CrowdStrike isolated the host after detecting malicious activity.
3. You work with the security team on remediation and service recovery, instead of troubleshooting the network connection or infrastructure.


## How can CrowdStrike threat intelligence help you identify which emerging threats affect your applications?


When a new threat emerges, teams need to know whether it affects their applications and which remediation actions matter most. Vulnerability severity alone does not establish that priority. Teams also need to consider runtime exposure and business impact.


Connecting CrowdStrike threat intelligence with Dynatrace runtime insights, such as findings from[Runtime Vulnerability Analytics](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/shortlink/vulnerability-analytics-hub) , helps teams assess relevant CVEs and indicators of compromise in their environment and prioritize remediation for exposed services.


## How does the Dynatrace integration with CrowdStrike work?


Dynatrace ingests CrowdStrike[detection findings](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/semantic-dictionary/model/security-events/detection#detection-finding) into Dynatrace Grail based on your configured collection schedule. It enriches those findings with runtime entities, such as cloud resources and hosts, so teams can see, for example, when a service disruption involves a host isolated by CrowdStrike.


The integration can also ingest CrowdStrike emerging[threat reports](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/shortlink/semantic-dictionary-security-events-threat-intelligence#threat-report) . Teams can compare reported CVEs and indicators of compromise with their runtime environment to identify exposed services and prioritize remediation.


CrowdStrike[audit logs](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/shortlink/semantic-dictionary-log-management-and-analytics#audit-logs) provide additional context for shared investigations. Available in Dynatrace, these logs help teams review changes to protection configurations and alerting profiles alongside runtime activity and service disruptions. Security and observability teams can use this context to investigate whether a configuration change contributed to an incident and coordinate follow-up actions.


## What can you do with the CrowdStrike integration?


After you set up the[integration](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/secure/threat-observability/security-events-ingest/ingest-crowdstrike-data) , you can use dashboards and Dynatrace apps to:


- **Review detections and coverage.** Security findings and coverage dashboards summarize CrowdStrike detections and show which monitored endpoints have CrowdStrike protection in place.
- **Track emerging threats.** Threat intelligence dashboards list the threats, threat actors, and indicators of compromise that CrowdStrike reports, so you can learn what CrowdStrike is seeing in the wild.
- **Investigate affected services.** The[Threats & Exploits app](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/shortlink/threats-exploits) shows each CrowdStrike detection in the context of the services and infrastructure it touches, which can help you tell whether an outage might have a security-related cause.
- **Review CrowdStrike configuration changes.** CrowdStrike audit logs in the[Logs app](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/shortlink/logs-app) let you check recent edits to protection policies and alert settings when you investigate an incident.
- **Ask questions in natural language.** AI-assisted analysis can help you query and summarize CrowdStrike findings in plain language. Review the results before using them to make operational decisions.

### Automate and orchestrate


You can also act on the data automatically. You can configure a workflow to send an email after Dynatrace receives a critical finding, so the SRE team can quickly see when a critical CrowdStrike detection affects a monitored host.


When CrowdStrike reports an emerging threat, a workflow can assess the related CVEs and indicators of compromise against Dynatrace runtime data and surface observed matches for review. The results help you understand potential exposure and prioritize remediation.
